# Lancashire - council briefing

*Auto-generated from council minutes, 27 April 2026 to 18 August 2026*

## What's dominating the agenda

Children & Education leads with 3,901 keyword hits, mostly via Cabinet and the Standing Advisory Council on Religious Education, followed by Finance & Budget (2,790, split between Cabinet, Audit, Risk and Governance, and Budget and Finance Scrutiny) and Local Economy (2,396, driven heavily by the Lancashire Combined County Authority, the county's devolution body). Note: although Lancashire is a highways authority, the statutory-notice committee filter used elsewhere in this app removed nothing here - no committee names matched the pattern, so this looks like a genuine agenda mix rather than an artefact. Also striking: 660 decisions logged in this window, but only 8 flagged as key - the rest are officer-delegated, with the Director of Highways and Transport (180) and Director of Growth and Property (96) alone accounting for over 40% of them, reflecting a large county-level operational caseload.

## Notable decisions

- The County Council responded to the government's "minded-to" decision on Local Government Reorganisation in Lancashire, following correspondence from the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (key decision, approved, 17 Aug).
- Cabinet approved refreshed strategies for Lancashire Archives and Local History, County Museums and Libraries services, covering 2026-2028 (key decision, 2 Jul).
- The Lancashire Combined County Authority approved allocating its devolved Post 16 Capacity capital fund and a Further Education Teacher Industry Exchange programme for construction (key decision, approved, 23 Jun).
- Cabinet approved Lancashire's SEND Reform Plan submission to the Department for Education (key decision, 4 Jun).
- Cabinet approved the Home to School Transport Policy for Lancashire families for the 2027/28 academic year (key decision, approved, 19 May).

## Worth a closer look

- Development Control Committee considered a planning application for a proposed Energy Recovery Centre at Hillhouse Business Park, Thornton-Cleveleys (10 Jun). [source](https://councilgateway.poteris.co.uk/council-api/documents/1458248/file)

## Projects on residents' radar

- **Kirkham town centre parking scheme** - Cabinet made permanent the waiting and loading restrictions trialled along Poulton Street, Preston Street, Freckleton Street, Church Street and Birley Street in Kirkham (19 May). [source](https://council.lancashire.gov.uk/ieDecisionDetails.aspx?ID=29969)
- **The Lancashire Way education strategy** - Cabinet approved a new Education Strategy for 2026-2028, replacing the previous 2022-2025 strategy for Lancashire schools (19 May). [source](https://council.lancashire.gov.uk/ieDecisionDetails.aspx?ID=29963)
- **Lancashire Integrated Transport Identity Strategy** - the Combined County Authority agreed a phased plan to bring bus, rail and other transport branding under a single Lancashire identity (23 Jun). [source](https://council.lancashire.gov.uk/ieDecisionDetails.aspx?ID=30384)
- **Lancashire Growth Plan** - the Combined County Authority's Overview and Scrutiny Committee reviewed progress on the Growth Plan, the county's economic strategy, against its performance framework (24 Jul). [source](https://councilgateway.poteris.co.uk/council-api/documents/1522849/file)
- **Champion Grants Scheme for Armed Forces and Veterans** - Cabinet considered a new grants scheme to support armed forces and veterans' community projects across the county (2 Jul). [source](https://councilgateway.poteris.co.uk/council-api/documents/1487306/file)
